title: Hybrid OTLP ↔ Prometheus ingestion with dynamic label bucketing and KPI stitching
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Background: Customers and internal services send a mix of Prometheus-style scrape metrics and OTLP-derived counters/histograms from inference runtimes. Current ingestion forks metrics into two processing paths which leads to duplicated storage, label explosions, and difficulty stitching per-request KPIs (latency/token-rate/error counts) across both streams.

Goal: Implement a unified hybrid ingest layer that accepts both Prometheus and OTLP payloads, normalizes labels using dynamic bucketing rules, and produces a consistent per-request KPI envelope for downstream SLI computation and dashboards. This should reduce cardinality, enable deterministic attribution for model/version/route, and simplify downstream alerting and cost accounting.

Scope: Design and implement an ingest adapter and lightweight enrichment pipeline deployed as the metrics gateway in front of our existing aggregation layer. Work includes schema design for the KPI envelope, label bucketing heuristics, rate-limited high-cardinality tag sampling, and a deterministic stitch key generation for correlating traces and metrics. Exclude long-term storage changes; those will be follow-ups.
success_criteria:
1) End-to-end ingest of Prometheus and OTLP metrics into the KPI envelope with <5% increased tail-latency on the gateway under 95th percentile load.
2) 40% reduction in high-cardinality metric streams seen in downstream aggregation (measured via cardinality sampling job).
3) Dashboards show aligned latency and error KPIs for route+model+version across both sources.
4) No regressions in existing SLO alerts during staged rollout.
technical_approach:
1) Ingest adapter accepts Prometheus remote_write and OTLP/multipart; both normalized to an internal event model.
2) Apply label bucketing rules: canonicalize host/service labels, map freeform tags to hashed bucket (configurable per label), and apply controlled sampling for user_id/session_id.
3) Generate a deterministic stitch_key using request_id || tenant || model_hash to correlate with traces.
4) Enrich events with runtime metadata (GPU family, quantization_profile, batch_size) using a local metadata cache.
5) Forward KPI envelope to the aggregation gateway and emit debugging diagnostics to a separate debug index for 72 hours.
6) Implementation will be in Go; use gRPC/HTTP2 for OTLP and a slim remote_write receiver for Prometheus.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (canary): deploy adapter to a single region by traffic-splitting 5% of non-critical routes for 2 weeks; validate metrics alignment and cardinality.
Phase B (ramped): 25% -> 60% over two weeks after fixes.
Phase C (cutover): flip default for new tenants and provide opt-in for legacy tenants for one month before full migration.
Rollback: route traffic back to legacy ingestion if KPI regression or gateway latency increase >20% sustained for 10m.
migration_plan: Provide a migration shim that tags events with legacy_stream_id during canary so downstream aggregation can join records. Run nightly reconciliation job to compare per-route KPI totals between legacy and hybrid pipelines; surface discrepancies >1%. Coordinate with Console team to freeze dashboard layout during migration window.
monitoring: Add Prometheus metrics for adapter request_latency_seconds (histogram), processed_events_total (counter by source), dropped_events_total (counter by reason), cardinality_estimate_gauge, and stitch_key_collision_count. Create dashboards: Hybrid Ingest Overview, Per-source KPI Alignment, High-Cardinality Alerting. Wire automated regressions to #infra-observability Slack and create a PagerDuty policy for >5% dropped events sustained 5m.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Label bucketing may under-index real customer dimensions -> Mitigation: make bucketing rules configurable per tenant and expose sampling controls in a secret config.
Risk: Stitch key collisions under heavy traffic -> Mitigation: use a composite of stable identifiers and add collision detection metric; on collision, fall back to best-effort attribution.
Risk: Increased gateway CPU from enrichment -> Mitigation: implement backpressure and time-budgeted enrichment; fall back to async enrichment if CPU saturated.
